basis: Malignant neoplasm involving the esophagus; metastatic sites are not defining or consistently involved.
Autoinflammatory syndrome defined by destructive sterile arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum and acne. Isolated colitis and blood findings do not establish common involvement.
Polyp located in the external auditory canal.
Hematopoietic dendritic-cell neoplasm; organ involvement varies by subtype. Immune-cell origin alone does not establish lymphoma or immune-mediated disease.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy in 4/4 patients. Weakness and amyotrophy reflect denervation rather than a primary muscle disorder.
Copper disorder with neuropathy/ID and ichthyosis; enteropathy ~100%. Cap excludes hearing loss (~83%), hepatic disease (~50%) and cataract (~33%).
Defined by arterial stenoses, skeletal fragility/malformations and learning or intellectual impairment (80–99%). Renal artery stenosis is vascular, without established renal damage.
Congenital fistula directly connects the rectum and bulbar urethra; both structures define the malformation.
Defining congenital abnormalities are absence of the tibia and deafness.
D-glycerate kinase deficiency causes organic aciduria; progressive encephalopathy occurs in 80–99%. Reduced hepatic enzyme activity alone is not liver damage.
Defined by scalp hair abnormalities, nail separation and cleft lip/palate; oral malformations map to gastrointestinal.
Congenital lower-lip fistula lined by oral mucosa, sometimes communicating with salivary glands. Infection is an occasional complication.
Skeletal growth disorder with delayed skeletal maturation and clinodactyly in 30–79%. Growth restriction alone does not establish endocrine disease; neurologic findings are occasional.
HIV infection directly impairs immunity. Opportunistic infections and associated organ diseases are separate diagnoses; no other organ qualifies across this umbrella.
Inherited protein C deficiency is a coagulation disorder. DVT (~44%) is a separately diagnosed thrombotic complication; common skin or eye damage is not established here.
Defined by osteosclerosis and brain malformations; cleft palate occurs in 80–99%, gingival disease in 30–79%. Pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 4/7 (~57%).
Benign fibrous neoplasm arising in bone, as established by its parent concepts.
Severe neurodevelopmental disorder with structural brain abnormalities; optic atrophy in 3/3. Other organ findings are isolated reports with insufficient frequency evidence.
Encephalitozoon infection; the supplied definition identifies brain and renal tubular lesions as common target-organ disease. Other listed sites lack frequency evidence.
Congenital cleft of the uvula, part of the oral soft palate. Nasal speech does not establish airway damage.
Heterotaxy with defining cardiac malformations; asplenia 2/3 and hydronephrosis 2/2 annotated. Small assessed samples limit certainty; visceral position alone is not damage.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in bone; bone origin, hematologic lineage and lymphoma mechanism all apply.
Inherited cardiac rhythm disorder with atrial fibrillation and premature atrial contractions.
Inflammation or degeneration of peripheral motor nerves. Secondary weakness does not establish direct muscle disease; immune mediation is not universal.
Multiple congenital intestinal atresias directly obstruct the bowel. Immunodeficiency belongs to a specific syndromic subtype rather than the umbrella.
